title: Temperature-Dependent Multiphysics Modeling of Additive Friction Stir Deposition Using Multi-Task Coupled Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) involves strongly coupled thermal and material-flow fields generated by frictional heating, severe plastic deformation, and tool-imposed boundary conditions. High-fidelity finite-volume methods (FVMs) can resolve these coupled fields accurately, but their computational cost limits repeated evaluation across process conditions. A separate modeling challenge arises from the strong temperature dependence of thermophysical properties. Treating thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat as constants can introduce substantial error in the predicted thermo-mechanical response. This work develops a steady-state multi-task coupled physics-informed neural network (MCoPINN) that predicts the three-dimensional velocity and temperature fields while reconstructing temperature-dependent thermophysical properties from sparse material data. A theoretical analysis formally decomposes the MCoPINN prediction error into contributions from property reconstruction and the neural field solver. A controlled one-dimensional nonlinear heat-conduction problem is first used to demonstrate this error decomposition and evaluate property reconstruction under sparse data. The framework is then applied to AFSD and evaluated against an FVM benchmark and experimental thermocouple measurements. MCoPINN reproduces the benchmark thermal and material-flow fields while improving the thermal prediction relative to the constant-property CoPINN. The benchmark FVM required

title: Inferring Soil Friction Angle from Robot Foot-Ground Force Histories: A Bayesian Inverse Approach to Proprioceptive Soil Sensing
abstract: Foot-ground interaction signals recorded by quadruped robots may enable spatially distributed, in situ characterization of soil strength. As a first step, we test whether the internal friction angle $ϕ$ of cohesionless soil can be identified from the force history of a simplified rotating leg. A two-dimensional continuum model implemented with the material point method, benchmarked against measured rotating-leg force histories, generates the training data, and two Gaussian-process surrogates support Bayesian inversion of the full histories. In matched-model experiments, the framework recovers 14 off-grid friction angles with a median absolute error of approximately $0.1^\circ$ (maximum $\sim 0.7^\circ$); the reported credible intervals contain the true value in every case. These results establish that $ϕ$ is identifiable when the forward model is correctly specified, and support further development of proprioceptive soil sensing for spatially variable terrain, with applications from physics-grounded world models for robot training to post-wildfire slope assessment.

title: Analysis of lap-shear force in automotive 22MnB5 boron steel sheet joints using friction stir spot welding
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering
abstract: Friction stir spot welding has shown potential for both similar- and dissimilar-material joints, positioning it as a promising alternative to resistance spot welding. Despite the importance of similar boron steel joints, recent studies on the friction stir spot welding (FSSW) of 22MnB5 steel have focused on dissimilar joints, especially those with aluminum alloys. In this context, similar FSSW lap joints in hot-stamped 22MnB5 steel offer opportunities to investigate the weld microstructure, lap-shear force, and failure modes. This study investigates the feasibility of joining 22MnB5 steel sheets using polycrystalline cubic boron nitride tools. The test sheets underwent thermal treatment to replicate the hardness of hot-stamped steel and were welded using two tool geometries to evaluate different pin diameters. A central composite design was employed to analyze the effects of welding parameters, rotation speed (727–2073 r/min), plunge rate (0.4–2.4 mm/s), and dwell time (2.6–9.4 seconds). Higher lap-shear forces were observed with the tool having a larger pin diameter and at high rotation speeds. The rotational speed was a significant variable in the model for both geometries. At the same time, plunge rate, dwell time, and their interaction were also statistically significant for the tool with a greater pin diameter. The lap-shear force and failure mode were directly related to the extent of the stirring zone. The minimum force requirement of 10.3 kN for resistance spot weldin

title: Coupled Physics Informed Neural Network (coPINN) as Standalone Multi-Physics Solver for Additive Friction Stir Deposition
abstract: Additive Friction Stir Deposition (AFSD) is a metal additive manufacturing process gaining increased attention due to its solid-state processing nature and the desirable properties it produces. Due to the multi-physics nature of the process, with complex coupled partial differential equations, computational modeling entails inaccuracies and slowness in utilizing numerical methods. This work proposes a coupled Physics Informed Neural Network (co-PINN) as a fast and accurate mesh-free solver for predicting the thermo-mechanical processing history of the AFSD process. Unlike a typical notion of data-driven neural networks, the co-PINN is an NN-based standalone solver for PDE-based models. The mesh-free nature of the method allows for better estimations of the gradient-based derived physical quantities at any given algorithmic step, such as the effective strain rate in the case study, eventually leading to a better solution. Motivated by a one-dimensional case of heat and mass transfer in a rod, the proposed co-PINN accurately predicts the material flow and temperature distribution for a steady-state coupled fluid dynamics and heat transfer model of the AFSD process in the Eulerian reference frame. The co-PINN-based solver has a low residual error and takes a fraction of the time (as low as 35 minutes) than the existing volume-based solver at an appropriate mesh level. title: A Two-Stage Self-Aligning, Two-Sided Flat-on-Flat Friction-Measurement Device for Universal Testing Machines Under Elevated Contact Pressures
abstract: The precise determination of the coefficient of friction is of fundamental importance in many engineering applications, especially in cases where different material pairs, surface-treated systems, polymers or coated surfaces come into contact with each other. Classical tables of friction data can often only be used as approximate values, since friction behavior is considerably influenced by surface pressure, sliding velocity, contact geometry and the condition of the surfaces. In this article, we present the principle, structural design and application possibilities of a new friction-measuring device that can be adapted to a universal testing machine (UTM). Our device provides a symmetric, two-sided flat-on-flat contact configuration, a closed loading system and a two-stage self-aligning mechanism, with adjustable normal load. The relevant rotational axes are positioned in the contact planes to reduce parasitic moments and the coupling between the tensile measuring force and the applied normal load, thereby reducing a potential source of measurement variability. With the device, both static and dynamic friction coefficients can be determined (and the transition ranges can be explored in detail), at different nominal contact pressures (p, up to 50 MPa) and sliding velocities (v, mm/min). title: The Institutional Encounter with SignalRupture: Category Mismatch, Epistemic Friction, Boundary Defense, Containment, Recognition, and Instrumental Adoption
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: New research architectures do not enter institutions as neutral information. Institutions already possess disciplinary boundaries, classifications, review systems, funding structures, measurement infrastructures, professional jurisdictions, legitimacy mechanisms, and established pathways for converting knowledge into action. SignalRupture creates an unusually difficult institutional-translation problem because it presents itself not as a single domain theory but as a master research architecture whose formal expression contains three coupled domain metatheories - Infrastructure Science, Meaning and Agency Science, and Experience and Value Science - alongside bounded fields, mechanisms, operators, measurements, cultural provenance, and diagnostic programmes. The SignalRupture Institutional Encounter Model (SR-IEM) specifies nine possible response states: Category Mismatch, Preliminary Dismissal, Boundary Defense, Epistemic Friction, Diagnostic Reassessment, Self-Model Disruption, Containment and Translation, Constraint-Induced Recognition, and Instrumental Reliance. These states are observable institutional conditions rather than assumed emotional reactions. Institutions may skip states, reverse direction, fragment internally, accept individual constructs while rejecting the architecture, reject SR for valid scientific reasons, independently reproduce similar concepts without influence, or never encounter SR at all. title: Fabrication and Characterization of AA7075/Al 2 O 3 /Graphene Hybrid Composites via Friction Stir Additive Manufacturing
abstract: Lightweight metal matrix composites (MMCs) are widely utilized across marine, defense, aerospace, and automotive sectors due to their high strength‐to‐weight ratio, wear resistance, stiffness, and thermal stability. This study investigates a hybrid composite of AA7075 reinforced with a constant total reinforcement of 10 wt%, while varying the individual weight percentages of graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) and aluminum oxide nanoparticles (Al 2 O 3 ). The composite was successfully fabricated via a multi‐layer friction stir additive manufacturing (FSAM). Among five different samples, the sample with 0.4 wt% GNPs and 9.6 wt% Al 2 O 3 shows significant improvements over the unreinforced base alloy: a 47.7% increase in tensile strength (230.8–340.83 MPa), a 32% improvement in Vickers hardness (67.6–89.33 HV), and a 24.6% increase in compressive strength (208.9–260.28 MPa) indicate the potential of FSAM to improve the structural and mechanical characteristics of the material. Microstructural characterization using field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE‐SEM) and optical microscopy (OM) confirms that the mechanical strength is significantly improved due to sound interlayer bonding and uniform reinforcement distribution within the stir zone. This study demonstrates a substantial improvement in mechanical properties, thereby increasing the suitability of the composite for industrial applications.

title: Influence of Friction Stir Welding and Post-Weld Aging on Corrosion Behavior of LPBF A20X Alloy
abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the production of high-strength A20X aluminum components with complex geometries for aerospace applications. However, the limited build volume of LPBF systems often requires separately manufactured parts to be joined. This study compares the microstructure and corrosion behavior of LPBF A20X under four material conditions: base material (BM), as-welded stir zone (SZ), solution-treated and peak-aged base material (BM–PA), and solution-treated and peak-aged stir zone (SZ–PA). Microstructural evolution was assessed using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction, while corrosion behavior was evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. Among the tested specimens, BM exhibited the lowest corrosion current density (0.703 μA/cm2), followed by SZ (0.966 μA/cm2), BM–PA (2.257 μA/cm2), and SZ–PA (3.181 μA/cm2). The impedance response and post-polarization SEM observations indicated lower corrosion resistance after solution treatment and aging, particularly in SZ–PA. These findings are consistent with a possible contribution from micro-galvanic interactions involving redistributed and precipitated Cu-rich constituents, TiB2 particles, and the Al matrix. Under the tested conditions, post-weld heat treatment reduced corrosion resistance compared to FSW alone. This underlines the need to optimize welding and heat-treatment parameters for LPBF A20X components.

title: Seismic performance of loose mortise and tenon joints strengthened by novel wooden friction damper and timber wedge: Experimental tests and numerical modelling
abstract: To improve the seismic resilience of loose M-T joints in ancient wooden building and mitigate their deterioration damage, this paper proposes a Que-ti shaped wooden friction damper specifically designed for reinforcing loose M-T joints. Six 1:3.2 scaled M-T joint specimens with various reinforcement parameters, including one non-damaged joint, one loose joint, and four reinforced joints repaired by damper and embedding wooden wedge, were fabricated and performed to the cyclic loading tests. The collaborative load-bearing mechanisms, failure modes, hysteresis behaviour, degradation laws of strength and rotational stiffness, and energy dissipation and deformation capacity of the specimens were analyzed. The test results indicated that the synergistic reinforcement effect between the damper and wooden wedge significantly reduced the tenon pull-out in the loose joint. Both the friction coefficient and bolt preload of the damper had significant effects on the initial flexural stiffness, load-carrying capacity, and ductility of the damaged M-T joints. Specifically, when the bolt’s preload remained at 3 kN, compared with loose joint, the reinforced M-T joint with a friction index of 0.5 exhibited up to 170% enhancement in positive moment-resisting, with the average initial rotational stiffness showing an increase of up to 46%, while the average ductility factor of the reinforced M-T joint with a friction index of 0.8 increased by up to 150%. title: Friction surfacing-based additive manufacturing of Ti–6Al–4V: process parameters, coating geometry, surface analysis, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior
abstract: Abstract In the present work, the solid state deposition of Ti–6Al–4V on grade 2 titanium substrates by friction surfacing was investigated. After initial parameter optimization to select adequate horizontal and vertical forward speeds, tests were conducted with rotational speeds of 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000 and 8000 rpm. The deposited material was subsequently characterized in terms of its overall geometry and surface texture, mechanical properties, microstructure and electrochemical corrosion resistance in Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS). Except for the coating obtained with 4000 rpm rotational speed, in all remaining cases deposits were relatively uniform and all coatings exhibited excellent bond strength—superior to the shear strength of the titanium substrate. The coatings exhibited elevated average hardness values ( $$\approx $$ 350 HV) and their microstructure was found to be composed mostly of needle-shaped $$\alpha $$ located at previous $$\beta $$ grain boundaries, with minor quantities of equiaxed $$\alpha $$ grains located near the substrate interface. No significant differences were noticed regarding the electrochemical behavior of the tested coatings, which exhibited similar corrosion resistance compared to the original base material, an indication of the reliability of the friction surfacing process for producing corrosion resistant coatings.

title: Analysis of tensile properties, fracture characteristics, and microstructural features in friction stir welding of dissimilar aluminium alloys reinforced with Al 2 O 3
abstract: In the present investigation, dissimilar aluminium alloys AA2014-T6 and AA5083-H111 were joined using friction stir welding combined with in-situ reinforcement of aluminium oxide (Al2O3) particles. A single V-groove with an included angle of 45° was machined along the welded joint line, into which Al2O3 particles were introduced prior to subsequent friction stir processing. The welded joints were subjected to three friction stir processing passes to promote effective material flow and particle dispersion. Microhardness measurements revealed values of up to 105 VHN in the stir zone, while tensile testing showed an improvement of up to 18% compared to the unreinforced joint. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations indicated the distribution of Al2O3 particles and effective mixing within the stir zone, and elemental mapping verified the presence of reinforcement across the processed region. Fractographic analysis indicated predominantly ductile fracture characterized by equiaxed dimples. Wear testing showed that the 9 wt.% Al2O3 condition exhibited the lowest wear rate among the investigated reinforcement levels.

title: Effect of stirring probe geometry on gap-bridging mechanisms and joint strength in wire-based friction stir welding of EN AW-2024 T351 Alclad
abstract: This study investigates the influence of stirring probe geometry on gap-bridging mechanisms, microstructure, and mechanical properties in wire-based friction stir welding (W-FSW) of EN AW-2024 T351 Alclad aluminium alloy. A multi-pin tool concept with continuous wire feeding was applied to enable the filling of large joint gaps during welding. Ten different probe geometries were systematically evaluated with respect to weld integrity, material flow, and resulting joint performance. The results demonstrate that a 4 mm joint gap, corresponding to 200% of the sheet thickness, can be successfully bridged using selected probe geometries. X-ray and metallographic analyses confirmed predominantly sound weld regions for the successful configurations. The probe geometry significantly affects material flow behaviour, grain refinement, and mechanical properties. Fine-grained, recrystallised microstructures with average grain diameter down to approximately 2.55 μ m and high fractions of high-angle grain boundaries were obtained. Hardness distributions exhibit the characteristic W-shaped profile known from conventional friction stir welding (FSW), with local minima on the retreating side. The highest mechanical performance was achieved using a probe geometry with upward-orientated triangular pins (P6), reaching 85% and 89% of the base material strength in transverse and longitudinal directions, respectively. title: The Fluid Dynamics of Systemic Defense Procurement: Managing Frictions and Legal Flows in Hybrid Warfare Contexts
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This study introduces a radical paradigm shift in the re-engineering of organizational structures and defense supply chains, analyzed through the combined framework of computational econophysics and Global Flow Law. Rejecting the static constraints of mere formal compliance, the model defines corporate and military architectures as open systems governed by predictive matrices. Using block diagram algebra, the transmissibility of material, technological, and financial resources is parameterized through the hydraulic conversion of the CARVER matrix variables. This methodological framework is specifically designed to optimize operational readiness and immunize the chain of command against bureaucratic viscosity, thereby preventing informational and contractual cavitation within contemporary asymmetric and urban warfare scenarios. Finally, the paper proposes the establishment of the "Triumvirate of the Flow" as an adaptive governance organ to manage the noosphere and the gray zone prior to the symmetrical escalation of systemic crises. [This paper constitutes a monographic advance section of a broader upcoming volume, representing the natural doctrinal evolution of the theoretical framework originally established in "Lo scacchiere (h)a un solo colore", Rome, Ciampi Ed., 2026].

title: Synergistic friction and wear reduction in CuSn10-modified basalt fiber-reinforced epoxy composites via protic ionic liquid and graphene nanolubrication
abstract: Abstract Basalt fiber-reinforced epoxy (BFRP) composites combine a favorable strength-to-weight ratio with relatively low cost, which makes them attractive for structural applications. However, the epoxy matrix has limited abrasion resistance, and this restricts how well these composites perform under sustained sliding contact. In this study, two autoclave-processed BFRP variants were tested: an unfilled composite (60 wt% basalt fiber) and a hybrid composite modified with 10 wt% CuSn10 bronze powder. The two samples were evaluated under dry sliding and under lubrication with four 2-hydroxyethylammonium (2-HEA)-based protic ionic liquid (PIL) nanofluids two used neat (MSu, MCi) and two dispersed with 0.1 wt% graphene (MSu + 0.1%G, MCi + 0.1%G). Pin-on-disc tests were performed under a normal load of 10 N and a sliding speed of 0.25 m·s⁻¹, and worn surfaces were characterized by SEM-EDS. All four PIL nanofluids reduced the steady-state coefficient of friction (COF) by 83–94% relative to dry sliding, while specific wear rate reductions ranged from 14% to over 99%, with the graphene-dispersed citrate PIL (MCi + 0.1%G) consistently yielding the best performance. Notably, the CuSn10-modified composite showed a wear rate comparable to the best-lubricated unfilled composite even under dry sliding, indicating that the bronze particles act as a load-bearing phase independent of lubrication. title: Post-weld heat treatment of AA7075 friction stir welded joints manufactured under various tool rotation speeds and cooling conditions
journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effect of post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) on the microstructure, microhardness, tensile properties, and fracture behavior of friction stir welded AA7075 joints produced under different cooling conditions (air, water, quenching oil, cutting fluid) and tool rotation speeds (600–1400 rpm). PWHT increased and homogenized microhardness, with the stir zone generally exhibiting higher hardness than the surrounding regions. Abnormal grain growth (AGG) occurred in the shoulder-driven zone of all specimens, irrespective of cooling condition or tool rotation speed, and was also observed in the pin-driven zone of most joints. For defect-free specimens, PWHT increased yield strength by more than 70% and ultimate tensile strength by approximately 35%, with the highest UTS values exceeding that of the base material. The air-welded joint also showed nearly doubled ductility and was the only heat-treated joint to fracture outside the weld region. Defective joints exhibited limited ductility. Fractography revealed intergranular cracking, dimpled transgranular fracture, particle-assisted microvoid formation, and strain localization. Overall, PWHT improved hardness and strength but did not prevent AGG, particularly in the shoulder-driven zone.

title: Microstructural stability and mechanical performance of friction stir and electron beam welded Al-Mg-Si joints subjected to post-welding heat treatment
abstract: This study reveals how fundamentally different weld thermal histories influence precipitate evolution, mechanical properties, and strain localization during post-welding heat treatment (PWHT). For this purpose, two welding techniques, solid-state friction stir welding (FSW) and the fusion joining technique, electron beam welding (EBW) were employed on a precipitate-hardened Al-Mg-Si alloy. Particular attention is given to the distinct responses of solid-state and fusion welding processes to subsequent thermal treatments and their implications for joint performance. Both welding techniques generated tensile residual stresses exceeding 130 MPa in the as-welded condition. However, the weld microstructures exhibited markedly different thermal stability during PWHT. In EBW joints, the fusion zone retained its coarse dendritic morphology (average size ∼34 μm), while the base material consisted of grains with an average size of ∼15 μm. In contrast, FSW produced a dynamically recrystallized stir zone with a fine-grained structure (∼2 μm), which remained stable during aging but experienced pronounced grain coarsening to approximately 300 μm after solution treatment and aging. This abnormal grain growth altered the fracture behavior, promoting grain-boundary fracture, whereas all other conditions exhibited ductile failure characterized by a dimpled morphology. title: STUDY OF ABRASIVE RESISTANCE OF POLYMERIC MATERIALS FOR SLIDING BEARINGS OF AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY
abstract: One of the most important ways to increase the reliability of agricultural machinery in the conditions of modern agriculture is the use of polymeric materials in its units and aggregates. In a large number of parts made of polymeric materials are used in modern harvesters, which is due to a number of technological and economic advantages of polymers over traditional metals. Slip supports are an important element of friction units in the harvester of agricultural harvesting equipment, in connection with which they are subject to intensive wear by abrasive particles, so parts for friction units must be made of durable materials. (Research purpose) The research purpose is developing effective solutions to improve the durability and reliability of the sliding supports by selecting the appropriate material, manufacturing technology and further modification of the selected material. (Materials and methods) Polyurethane NOACAST 700 was used as a research material, the abrasive resistance of which was investigated on an abrasimeter by the Taber method. The measurement method was based on the measurement of the loss of mass of the sample under mechanical action. (Results and discussion) It was substantiated that manufacturing technology affects wear resistance, samples obtained by injection molding wear less compared to samples made by free casting (51 vs 56 percent, respectively). title: Experimental and numerical investigation of failure behavior in hybrid adhesive bonded/friction stir spot welded AA6082/AZ31 dissimilar joints
abstract: The present study investigates the mechanical performance, failure behavior, and numerical modeling of a novel hybrid adhesive bonding (AB) friction stir spot welding (FSSW) joining technique for AA6082 aluminum and AZ31 magnesium alloys. The objective was to develop a hybrid joint capable of achieving the high strength of adhesive bonding while minimizing the detrimental thermal and mechanical effects of FSSW on the adhesive layer. Several lap joint configurations were manufactured and evaluated, including AB-only, FSSW-only, and hybrid AB+FSSW joints with different weld locations. Mechanical performance was evaluated using tensile-shear tests, while microstructural characterization was conducted using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and micro-hardness measurements. Finite element (FE) models incorporating cohesive zone modeling for the adhesive layer and ductile fracture criteria for the weld region were developed and validated experimentally. Results showed that FSSW-only joints exhibited the lowest mechanical performance, while the hybrid joint with the weld located at the center of the overlap achieved an average maximum load of 9.95 kN, approaching that of the AB-only joint (10.93 kN). After refining the numerical spot-weld geometry based on experimental observations, the numerical predictions correctly captured the fracture location and overall trends across all joint configurations, although quantitative accuracy was lower for the FSSW-only joints. title: Mechanical and nanomechanical characterization of Al 2014-ZrO 2 /TiC surface composites fabricated via underwater friction stir additive manufacturing
abstract: This study aims to explore fabrication and mechanical characterization of a 3-layer surface composite fabricated using underwater friction stir additive manufacturing (UFSAM) of Al2014-ZrO 2 /TiC material. The process was performed with different rotational speeds (1000, 1100 and 1200 rpm) and transverse speeds (40, 50 and 60 mm/min). The fabricated specimens were tested for the tensile strength and Vickers hardness, for the tensile strength and Vickers hardness, which were maximum at 446 ± 4.6 MPa and 156 ± 3.5 HV, respectively, at the optimum values of 1100 rpm rotational speed and 50 mm/min. The following nanomechanical properties were obtained hardness (138 ± 4.5 to 156 ± 3.5HV), elastic modulus (72.4 to 80.6 GPa), elastic recovery (23.8 to 30.7%), H/E ratio (0.0250 to 0.0269), H 3 /E 2 ratio (0.00113 to 0.00166), maximum penetration depth (hmax = 288 nm), and residual/final depth (hf-186 nm). The effect of the strain rate on the indentation response was also investigated ranging from 0.005 to 1.000 s -1 . An indentation size effect (ISE) was also noticed at all strain rates. The underwater processing environment further promoted rapid heat dissipation, which restricted excessive grain growth and contributed to microstructural refinement. A series of jump strain-rate tests showed a typical sawtooth-type hardness response, with small, instantaneous jumps in hardness with each increase in strain rate, suggesting strain-rate sensitivity in the deformation mechanism. title: Experimental Investigation on Constructions and Materials Observed by Digital Image Processing
journal: NATO science for peace and security series. D, Information and communication security
abstract: This study focuses on the capabilities of the Digital Image Correlation technique to measure displacement and deformation fields in a wide range of applications, from structural health monitoring of large-scale objects to nanoscale observations in materials testing for determining the properties of newly developed materials. The importance of strain-sensitive patterns and the problems associated with monitoring a large surface area while simultaneously adjusting the image scale to focus observation exclusively on the site of maximum deformation are considered. The structural health monitoring experiments include the investigation of a full-size timber wall under simulated seismic loading and a test setup according to the ISO 21581 standard, as well as full-scale metallic cantilevered pylons for highway lighting posts loaded by multiple-cycle pushover tests at a low frequency and small amplitude. From a materials testing perspective, further tests were conducted on newly developed composite materials for applications in areas subjected to high friction and mechanical loads, including engineering equipment, transportation systems, and bearings, where optimal combinations of low friction, high strength, and wear resistance are required. The Digital Image Correlation technique was used to obtain a complete picture of the displacement and deformation fields across the monitored surface of the tested constructions and specimens.

title: Conclusion and Future Trends on the use of Interlayer Materials for the Joining of Aluminium Alloys Using FSW and FSSW
abstract: This chapter presents the current state of the use of interlayer materials using friction stir welding (FSW) and friction stir spot welding (FSSW). It has been demonstrated that the use of interlayer materials positively or negatively affects the resulting properties of the fabricated welds or spot welds during FSW and FSSW of similar and dissimilar materials. These two welding techniques are used for the solid-state joining of numerous materials, such as aluminium, copper, and magnesium. In order to expand the use of interlayer materials such as copper and zinc, more studies are needed, and that will lead to their optimization. It has been shown that, in some cases, interlayer materials in powder form meaningfully influenced the thickness, morphology, and type of formed intermetallic compounds (IMCs), while the interlayer materials in sheet form exhibited different properties when compared with welds fabricated using conventional friction stir welding and friction stir spot welding. It is therefore imperative that more types of interlayer materials should be utilised and extensively studied to make a significant contribution to the body of knowledge.

title: Evaluation of Tribological Behaviors of Lightweight Crosshead Materials in a Reciprocating Plunger Pump
abstract: Lightweight design is crucial for reducing inertial forces and vibrations in high-power-density reciprocating plunger pumps (RPPs). However, the tribological compatibility of lightweight alloys for crosshead–liner tribo-pairs is not well understood. This study systematically evaluates the friction and wear behaviors of six lightweight materials (TC4, TC4 (MAO), TC11, TC18, ZL108, and AlSi10Mg) sliding against HT250 gray cast iron under different lubrication conditions using an SRV IV tribometer. The results show that the lubrication regime significantly affects tribological performance. Water lubrication led to severe abrasive wear and high friction coefficients (0.75–0.91), while oil lubrication reduced friction to around 0.20 and promoted the formation of protective boundary films rich in P, S, and Zn. Material selection played a key role in wear mechanisms: aluminum alloys performed better under oil lubrication, whereas titanium alloys were more stable under water-lubricated conditions. MAO treatment on TC4 improved wear resistance, reducing the wear weight to less than 0.3 mg under oil lubrication by creating a strong ceramic oxide layer. Negative wear rates in lower specimens indicated material transfer from the upper specimen to the lower specimen. Based on performance metrics, the TC4-MAO/Shell 220 combination is recommended for lightweight crosshead applications. This study offers insights and guidelines for material selection to enhance the reliability and efficiency

title: Influence of Tib2 Reinforcement and Tool Traverse Speed on the Structural and Thermal Behavior of Dissimilar Metals (AA7075–AA2024) of Friction Stir Welded Joints: an ABAQUS Study
journal: i-manager s Journal on Material Science
abstract: Friction Stir Welding (FSW) is a modern solid-state joining technique known for its energy efficiency, strong joints, and minimal environmental impact. This project focuses on joining two dissimilar high-strength aluminium alloys AA7075 and AA2024 using the simulation software ABAQUS. The welding was performed on the plates measuring 200 mm in length, 60 mm in width, and 6 mm in thickness. In this study, a Finite Element (FE) simulation was performed to understand the structural and thermal behaviour during welding. Various process parameters were tested, including tool rotational speed, feed rate and tilt angle to identify the most effective settings for achieving strong and defect-free joints. The simulation showed that the welding parameters were Tool speeds of 1000,2000 and 3000 rpm; Feed rates of 1,2 and 3 mm/sec; Tilt angles of 10,1.50 and 2°. These parameters produced in a moderate peak temperature of approximately 580°C, which is within the ideal plasticization range for both AA7075 and AA2024 without exceeding their melting points. This ensures proper material flow, defect-free weld formation, and maintenance of the mechanical properties.

title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical behavior of EN AW-2014A (AlCu 4 SiMg)/SiC reinforced composites under friction stir welding
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering
abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) was used to join stir-cast EN AW-2014A aluminum matrix composites reinforced with 5, 10, and 15 wt.% SiC, under fixed process parameters (270 r/min, 78 mm/min, 2° tilt). This work provides the first systematic, zone-resolved analysis linking SiC weight fraction to material flow, weld-zone microstructural evolution, hardness distribution, tensile behavior, and fracture response in FSW of EN AW-2014A composites, establishing an integrated structure–property–process relationship across reinforcement levels. Microstructural evolution across the heat-affected zone (HAZ), thermo-mechanically affected zone (TMAZ), and weld nugget was characterized by optical and scanning electron microscopy and correlated with microhardness and tensile properties. Welds were macroscopically free of gross defects, though microscale voids, particle-free regions, and SiC clustering were observed, increasing with reinforcement content. The 10 wt.% composite produced the most uniform nugget, with a fine, equiaxed grain structure suggestive of dynamic recrystallization and uniform SiC dispersion; 5 wt.% showed limited particle breakup, while 15 wt.% showed agglomeration and voids from high flow resistance. Nugget microhardness rose substantially over the as-cast condition: 95.16 to 127.20 HV, 123.68 to 140.12 HV, and 133.36 to 150.19 HV for 5, 10, and 15 wt.%, respectively (approximately 34%, 13%, and 13% improvement). The HAZ was consistently the softest zone, likely associate

title: Strategic partnership maintenance under geopolitical friction: a composite-indicator analysis of China–Malaysia relations, 2015–2024
abstract: Strategic partnerships can remain economically dense even when the institutional channels that keep cooperation workable weaken. This article develops the Strategic Partnership Maintenance Composite Index (SPMCI), a formative measure of observable maintenance activity rather than latent trust, alignment, or resilience. It applies the index to China–Malaysia relations from 2015 to 2024 using eight indicators across economic, political, security, and societal dimensions. Formal relationship status is kept outside the composite to separate diplomatic labeling from realized maintenance activity. The baseline records 66.4 in 2015, reaches a low of 19.4 in 2020, remains weak through 2022, and rises to 71.5 in 2024. The broad 2020–2022 trough and 2023–2024 recovery survive leave-one-indicator-out tests, equal dimension weights, alternative scaling choices, document-count sensitivities, and the exclusion of pandemic-sensitive mobility indicators, although exact annual ordering changes under some specifications. The 95% Dirichlet intervals are treated as weight-sensitivity bounds rather than statistical confidence intervals. Economic exchange provides a material floor, while political and security channels vary more sharply with the surrounding relationship environment. The results support a narrow claim: formal partnership status can persist while the observable channels that sustain cooperation change substantially over time.

title: Sensor-based monitoring and machine learning modelling for predicting the mechanical properties of friction stir welded Al 6061-Cu 11000 dissimilar joints
abstract: The engineering properties of dissimilar metals like Aluminum and Copper have led to their increased use of Frictional Stir Welding (FSW) of both materials in electrical, automotive, and energy-storage applications. However, it is still a challenge to obtain good-quality FSW joints with good mechanical properties because of the complicated thermal and mechanical interactions that occur during the welding process. This study presents a low-cost sensor-based monitoring and machine-learning framework for the prediction of parameters for FSW of dissimilar metals. The integration of real-time sensor-based monitoring for data acquisition enabled the development of machine learning models for predicting the mechanical properties of FSW Al 6061-Cu 11000 joints. A modified milling machine equipped with an integrated Arduino-based acquisition system was developed to continuously record key welding parameters, including rotational speed, travel speed, plunge depth, tilt angle, axial force, torque, and peak temperature. Experimental welding trials were conducted to generate the dataset linking process parameters with ultimate yield strength (YS), tensile strength (UTS), and hardness (HV). To capture the changing dynamics of the system, four machine learning models (linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost) were used to fit the dataset for mechanical property prediction that maps the input and output variables. The predictive model with the best performance had a r

title: Public Credit Guarantees, Financial Frictions, and Macroeconomic Stabilization: Evidence from Italy in the 2020–2022 Emergency Period
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: CLIFF SGR Research Center Working Paper No. 2026-01. This version was presented at the International Conference in Banking and Financial Studies (ICBFS 2026), University of Parma, 10 September 2026. A revised version is in preparation. Comments are welcome: research@cliffsgr.it. Abstract. This paper examines the macroeconomic role of the public credit guarantee schemes adopted in Italy during the 2020-2022 emergency period. Since no available study identifies a direct elasticity between guarantees and GDP, the analysis proceeds in two steps. First, it consolidates and subjects to a coherence comparison the firm-level treatment effects estimated by other authors, showing that two independent studies, based on different datasets, converge on a credit additionality of roughly 0.6-0.85 euro per euro of guaranteed amount. Second, it proposes an original scenario-based aggregation exercise that applies the marginal effects to the volumes of loans approved under the Central Guarantee Fund (about 226 billion euro net of moratoria, the main scenario) and, in an extended out-of-sample scenario, also to those of the SACE Garanzia Italia scheme, for about 268 billion euro in total. The exercise is preceded by a dimensional compatibility check between the units of the coefficients, the denominators, the time dimension and the reference population, and yields an annual investment-flow differential in 2022 of about 38-46 billion euro and an end-2022 employment-stock differential of about 34

title: Numerical Investigation on the Effect of Weld Spot Location on the Mechanical Performance and Adhesive–Weld Interaction in Hybrid Adhesive-Bonded/Friction-Stir-Spot-Welded AA6082/AZ31 Joints
first_author: Luís Diogo Vidal Saraiva Ribeiro Peixoto
abstract: Hybrid joining methods combining adhesive bonding (AB) and friction stir spot welding (FSSW) have attracted increasing attention for lightweight multi-material structures due to their potential to combine the advantages of both techniques. In this study, a numerical investigation of hybrid AB + FSSW joints for dissimilar AA6082 aluminum and AZ31 magnesium alloys was conducted using finite-element analysis. Three joint types were considered: adhesively bonded (AB), friction-stir-spot-welded (FSSW), and hybrid AB + FSSW joints. The influence of weld location and adhesive type on joint performance, failure behavior, and stress distribution was evaluated. Cohesive zone modeling was employed to simulate adhesive failure, while the modified Mohr–Coulomb ductile fracture criterion was used to predict fracture in the metallic substrates and weld regions. Two structural adhesives with distinct mechanical characteristics, Araldite AV138 and Nagase XNR6852 E-3, were considered. The results showed that the hybrid configuration with the weld located at the center of the overlap and the Nagase adhesive provided the most favorable performance, reaching a maximum load of approximately 9.4 kN, comparable to that of the adhesively bonded joint. In contrast, FSSW-only joints exhibited lower load-bearing capacity and predominantly failed through the weld interface. Stress analysis suggested that the adhesive layer significantly reduced stress concentrations around the weld spot, particularly whe

title: Process Parameter Optimization in Refill Friction Stir Spot Welding of 6061-T6 Aluminum Alloy and AZ31B-H24 Magnesium Alloy Dissimilar Joints
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
abstract: Lightweight multi-material structures that pair aluminum with magnesium are increasingly sought in the transport and aerospace sectors, yet sound dissimilar Al–Mg joints remain difficult to obtain because the two metals readily form hard, brittle Al–Mg intermetallic compounds (IMCs) whose growth along the bond line degrades joint strength. Refill friction stir spot welding (RFSSW) is a keyhole-free, solid-state process well suited to limiting this reaction, but a validated, quantitative process window for the AA6061-T6/AZ31B-H24 couple is still lacking. This study addresses that gap by establishing quantitative correlations between the governing RFSSW parameters, namely tool rotational speed (1800–2400 rpm), sleeve penetration depth (2.2–2.6 mm) and welding time (4–6 s), and the resulting thermal field, joint integrity and mechanical performance. A two-dimensional axisymmetric, fully coupled thermomechanical finite element model was developed in Simufact Forming 2025.2 software and validated against embedded K-type thermocouple and infrared thermography measurements, with the predicted and measured peaks agreeing to within about 5% (168 °C at 4 s and 216 °C at 6 s, recorded 5 mm from the weld center). The validated model predicts stir-zone peak temperatures of 320–498 °C across the process window; these remain below the solidus of both base alloys (582 °C for AA6061-T6 and 566 °C for AZ31B-H24), confirming a bulk solid-state process, while at the hottest settings, the interfa

title: "Better Lubrication Means Less Friction" Holds Only on the Near Side of the Minimum ── Adding a boundary term, which fades as the film thickens, to a fluid term, which grows with it, gives a friction coefficient with a minimum of 0.008686 at a film thickness of x=5.730000 ── the separator is whether the film is thicker than the roughness of the surfaces ── [Paper 711]
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Better lubrication is supposed to mean less friction. But the friction coefficient has a minimum, and beyond it better lubrication means more. Where that minimum lies, and why it exists at all, is counted here by separating two terms. No new theorem or law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new theorem or law is claimed──the Stribeck curve, the distinction between boundary and fluid-film lubrication, and the minimum of the friction coefficient are all standard (Stribeck 1902, Hamrock et al. 2004). No real bearing is claimed──a boundary friction of 0.10 and a fluid coefficient of 0.001 are representative values and move greatly with material, oil and load. No Stribeck number is constructed──speed, viscosity and load are not combined; only a dimensionless measure x of film thickness is used, and the position of the valley depends on how x is scaled. Wear and heat are not treated──the progress of wear, the temperature rise from friction and the action of additives are not treated. Nothing is fitted──no fit to a measured Stribeck curve is made; only the form of a sum of two terms is examined. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 710 showed that when return is proportional to size and cost grows as the 1.5 power, an optimal size appears strictly inside──there the sum of two terms produced a hill. title: Impact of Dust Deposition on Different Material Surfaces on Energy Systems
abstract: This research explores how different surface materials affect how dust collects on solar panels—an issue that often reduces solar energy output, especially in dry, dusty areas. The change of particle sizes was measured as well, and the results showed that the amount of dust collected did not simply depend on how rough a surface was. Instead, the material made a difference, but in ways that were not always predictable. The movement of dust layers or their getting stuck during tilting is also studied. This process helped us determine how gravity and friction affect dust sliding off panels. In some cases, up to 76% of the dust could be removed by flipping the panel upside down. These findings offer helpful guidance for solar power setups, helping designers choose the best materials and angles to reduce dust buildup or, in some cases, encourage certain particles to stick for special uses. Overall, the study helps improve solar energy performance in places where dust is constantly challenging. The compound of particles and fibers that is contaminated on a sheet of glass at different angles (50 o , 70 o , 80 o , 90 o , 120 o , 140 o , and 180 o ) as well as the amount of dust slipping was also measured.

title: Nonlinear wave dynamics and structural response of hybrid nanocomposite open shells under aerodynamic forces on a friction-coupled elastic foundation
abstract: It is extremely important to have information about the stability and wave propagation characteristics of the aircraft structure due to high-speed aerodynamic loads in order to design the next generation of flight vehicles. In this research work, a new coupled methodology between aerodynamics and foundation for nonlinear dispersion of a doubly curved nanocomposite fuselage panel in a supersonic flow regime is proposed. The material is made of an epoxy-based matrix reinforced by nanocrystalline alumina and is resting on a viscoelastic foundation with consideration of all possible interaction forces. Unlike the traditional aeroelastic theory, the proposed methodology offers a physically sound modification to the classical first-order supersonic piston theory. As a result, the aerodynamic loading is state-dependent and inherently dependent on the supporting medium, and the model naturally reduces to classical piston theory in the absence of any foundation effects. The deformation kinematics of the structure are formulated based on higher-order shear deformation theory having a hyperbolic shear strain distribution, while the geometric nonlinearity in the model has been accounted for by means of von Kármán strain-displacement relations. Hamilton’s principle is utilized to develop the fully coupled nonlinear governing equations, and these governing equations have been validated by making extensive comparisons with published results as well as by a separate finite element formulatio

title: Selection of polymeric materials for replacement sliding components used in internal combustion engine timing systems based on selected operational factors
abstract: This paper presents a study on the selection of polymeric materials (PA 6G, PA 6G+MoS₂, and PE 1000) for replacement sliding elements in internal combustion engine timing systems. The influence of operational parameters – such as dry friction, friction in a PMO 5W-40 oil bath at 20C and 90C, and the degree of oil aging and contamination – was analyzed. Using microindentation, profilometry, and oil particle analysis, the mechanical and tribological properties of the materials were evaluated. Oil lubrication significantly reduces the coefficient of friction; however, elevated temperatures and lubricant degradation increase wear. The results indicate that PA 6G+MoS₂ is the optimal replacement material for timing chain guides, with regular engine oil changes being crucial to maintaining component durability.

title: Effects of Substrate Material, Surface Preparation, and Operating Conditions on the Surface Characteristics and Tribological Performance of MoS2 Dry Film Lubricants
abstract: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) dry film lubricants (DFLs) are widely used in aerospace mechanisms when conventional liquid lubricants are impractical. While the effects of environment on MoS2 are well established, the influence of substrate characteristics and operating conditions remains less understood. In this work, three commercial MoS2-based DFLs (Lube-Lok 4396, Everlube 620C, and Everlube 9002) were applied to five aerospace-relevant substrate materials and characterized in terms of surface roughness, flatness, coating thickness, friction, wear life, and load-carrying capacity. Vendor surface preparation and DFL deposition increased roughness, reduced flatness, and shifted the surface toward a more peak-dominated morphology, with the magnitude of these changes depending on both the substrate and coating. Tribological performance was evaluated for a subset of the samples which showed that friction was substantially lower in dry nitrogen than in ambient air, increasing contact pressure reduced friction, and sliding speed had little effect. Lube-Lok 4396 exhibited the longest wear life and highest load-carrying capacity, while Everlube 620C exhibited the lowest friction. Measured friction, wear life, and load-carrying capacity also differed from vendor specifications. These results highlight the effects of substrate material, surface preparation, and operating conditions on the surface characteristics and tribological performance of commercial MoS2 DFLs for aerospace applicat

title: Replication materials for ENEECO-D-26-01536: Green Credit under Carbon Price Risk
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Executable replication materials for “Green Credit under Carbon Price Risk:Financing Frictions, Banking Market Power, and Firm Emissions”. The archivepreserves the original scientific script, calibration record, data for Figures1–8 and Appendix Tables C1–C4, and reference figures. It adds portable execution,pinned dependencies, parameter and output mapping, and verification tools.

title: Analysis and Calibration of DEM Parameters for Rock Materials Based on Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: The accuracy of discrete element method (DEM) simulations depends on the appropriate selection of microscopic parameters. However, conventional calibration using biaxial tests requires repeated adjustment of microscopic parameters until the macroscopic responses of numerical specimens match the target responses, making the process cumbersome and computationally demanding. In this regard, this study presents an interpretable, surrogate-assisted machine-learning framework for analyzing and calibrating DEM parameters of brittle rock materials represented by the Hertz–Mindlin bonded contact model. Decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were selected to compare single-tree and ensemble-tree regression approaches for capturing the nonlinear relationships between three microscopic parameters—friction coefficient μ, bond tensile strength Tb, and bond cohesion Cb—and two macroscopic parameters, bulk cohesion Co and internal friction angle φ. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was subsequently employed to quantify and interpret the contributions of individual microscopic parameters. XGBoost showed the best performance for predicting the macroscopic parameters, whereas Tb was less reliably predicted than μ and Cb. SHAP indicated that Cb and Tb contributed most strongly to Co, while μ dominated φ. Finally, differential evolution (DE) was combined with the forward prediction model to search for feasible microscopic parameter combinations reproduc

title: Modeling of instability in cemented granular materials with an enhanced multiscale model
abstract: Micromechanics of cemented granular materials provides a critical perspective for analyzing their complex macroscopic behavior, particularly regarding the progressive degradation of microscopic inter-particle bonds. Different from phenomenological approaches, multiscale modeling offers a powerful framework for linking grain-scale mechanics to macroscopic material responses. Building upon the previously developed two-dimensional H -bond model, this study introduces statistical heterogeneity in inter-particle bond strengths and combines it with previously proposed configurational reactions to describe progressive bond failure and post-breakage mesostructural reconfiguration. By mathematically formulating bonded contact stiffness, progressive bond damage, and the ultimate transition toward purely frictional behavior, the model seamlessly upscales these micro-mechanisms to the representative elementary volume (REV) level via statistical homogenization. The numerical results show that the H -bond model reproduces key qualitative features of the essential macroscopic signatures of cemented granular materials under given loading paths, providing insight into the link between bond degradation and macroscopic response. To extend its applicability to boundary value problems, the proposed framework is implemented as a VUMAT subroutine within Abaqus/Explicit. Leveraging this computational capability to simulate a particular landslide, the analysis demonstrates that progressive bond degra

title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
abstract: Abstract Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Investigation of the tribological properties of modified composite materials used under abrasive wear conditions
abstract: This study investigates the tribological properties and microstructural characteristics of modified composite materials designed for operation under abrasive wear conditions. The composite materials were prepared using an ED-20 epoxy resin base, modified with bismaleimide, furfuryl alcohol, AKT-10 grade Angren kaolin, and PEK modifiers. Select samples were also reinforced with glass and silk fibers. The samples were prepared under laboratory conditions, undergoing vacuum degassing and thermal curing processes. Tribological tests were conducted using the pin-on-disk method in accordance with ASTM G99 and ISO 7148 standards. Throughout the study, the coefficient of friction, mass loss, and specific wear rate were determined to evaluate the materials' resistance to abrasive wear.

title: Mechanical and tribological performance of bio-based polyamide/nanocellulose composites as sustainable engineering materials
abstract: Nanocellulose as filler gained interest in recent times due to its exceptional strength and reinforcement capabilities. Moreover, it is abundant, renewable, and affordable compared to other commonly used fossil-based reinforcements. However, research regarding its impact on the friction and wear of thermoplastic polymers is limited, despite proven benefits for the mechanical strength of composites. In this work, polyamide 11, a fully bio-based polyamide, was reinforced with 3 wt% or 5 wt% nanocellulose to produce sustainable engineering polymer composites as alternative to less environmentally friendly materials. These were evaluated regarding thermal, mechanical and microstructural properties, and tribological performance. The incorporation of nanocellulose led to an improvement of compressive strength by almost 25 %, while also increasing the crystallinity and glass transition temperature. The composites maintained a higher storage modulus of up to 1434.9 MPa for the composite with 5 wt% nanocellulose at elevated temperatures compared to 1350.5 MPa of neat polyamide 11 at room temperature. Tribological experiments showed that the addition of 3 wt% nanocellulose caused a reduction of the wear coefficient by almost 90 %. The coefficient of friction was lowered as well from 0.158 to 0.132. A change in tribofilm appearance was observed between the neat polyamide 11 and the composites, suggesting a difference in wear mechanisms. Furthermore, the non-destructive evaluation of tri

title: Innovative Design of a Brake Shoe Holder and Finite Element Analysis of the Contact Pressure Between the Wheel and the Brake Shoe
journal: Journal of the Korean society for railway
abstract: The frictional force of the wheel tread brake is governed by the contact pressure and the coefficient of friction between the two contacting surfaces. Uneven pressure distribution can cause temperature variations, heat spots, and thermal cracks on both the wheel and the friction material. It can also lead to uneven wear, shortening the service life of the wheel and brake shoe, and increasing maintenance costs. This study aimed to design an innovative brake shoe holder that achieves a more uniform contact pressure distribution between the wheel and the brake shoe. To evaluate the contact pressure, a finite element model comprising the brake shoe holder, brake shoe, and wheel was constructed, and numerical analyses were performed for brake shoe holders of various shapes. The proposed design reduced the maximum contact pressure and significantly increased the contact area between the wheel and the brake shoe friction material.

title: Becoming regenerative: A recursive and practice-driven process of social and material change
abstract: Regenerative agriculture (RA) is increasingly promoted as a strategy to restore soil health, enhance biodiversity, and strengthen climate resilience, yet what is less understood is how the process of transitioning toward RA is shaped and reshaped through influences from within and without. Drawing on practice theory, we examine farmers' RA transition processes through a qualitative study of 13 regenerative farms, five expert interviews, and three field visits. We find that RA transition unfolds as a recursive, ongoing, and socially embedded process in which farmers continuously reconfigure the images, skills, and material arrangements that constitute increasingly regenerative farming practices. This transition revolves around the core process of Becoming Regenerative and is surrounded by three interrelated dynamics: Making it Work , Knowing it's Working , and Claiming Visibility . The study contributes to research on RA by conceptualizing the transition as an ongoing practice shaped by change from within farmers' evolving roles and practices and from without through engagement and friction with competing practices of conventional farming. We further provide policy recommendations for supporting farmers throughout the early stages of the transition toward RA.

title: Application and Evaluation of the Material Point Method for Low-Velocity Asteroid Collisions Involving Large Deformations
abstract: The collisional lifetimes of asteroids larger than $\sim 10$ km in the present-day main belt are estimated to exceed the age of the solar system, suggesting that their shapes may preserve memories of the collisional environment in the primordial solar system. Recent studies performed systematic simulations of equal-mass and low-velocity ($50$--$400\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$) collisions between 50-km-radius asteroids using Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH), identifying the impact conditions that produce irregular shapes. As an alternative approach, we here employ the Material Point Method (MPM), a particle-grid method well suited to large deformation of solids and free from tensile instability, and we assess its applicability to such systems by direct comparison with the established SPH results. We integrate a previously established rock model combined with a fracture model, the Tillotson equation of state, and Drucker-Prager friction, with the efficient non-associative Drucker-Prager plasticity solver originally developed for granular flows. We perform 135 collision simulations of equal-mass rocky asteroids spanning 15 impact velocities ($50$--$400\,\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$) and 9 impact angles ($5$--$45^\circ$), following the setup of the previous SPH simulations. The mass, axis ratio, and shape classification of the largest remnants closely reproduce the trends of the previous SPH simulations. Since most material transitions into a granular state early in the collision, this agreemen

title: Percolation models for describing the thermal conductivity of polymer struc-tural materials
journal: Izvestiya of Kabardino-Balkarian State Agrarian University named after V M Kokov
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of thermal conductivity of structural polymer materials used in friction units of agricultural machinery. During operation, the working bodies and movable joints experience excessive heat. As a result, destructive processes can develop in their volume, leading to the failure of mechanisms and structures. Therefore, without a quantitative description of the thermal conductivity of polymer composites, their practical application is impossible. For this purpose, the percolation model is used in this work. Within the framework of percolation theory, models of a random superconducting grid (RSG) and a random grid of resistors (RGR) are proposed. It is shown that the first model is applicable to the description of thermal conductivity of carbon fiber plastics based on phenylene below the percolation threshold, and the second above the percolation threshold. It turns out that in both cases the coefficient of thermal conductivity agrees fairly well with the theoretical estimate, i.e. their linear correlation is observed. The results obtained make it possible to clarify the physical nature of the heat transfer mechanisms corresponding to the RSG and RGR models. In the case of RSC, heat transfer through the fibers is realized instantly and therefore the amount of thermal conductivity is limited by heat transfer through the sections of the polymer matrix separating the fibers. In the RGR model, heat transfer is realized through the contact points of

title: Methodological aspects of measuring the electrostatic field strength of polymer building materials
abstract: Introduction. The advancement in the chemical industry has led to the development of a broad spectrum of synthetic polymer materials. Their exceptional performance characteristics, combined with the capability to engineer materials with tailored properties, facilitate their extensive application in industrial manufacturing. However, the propensity of polymer surfaces to accumulate electrostatic charge presents potential risks of adverse health effects for end-users, necessitating systematic monitoring and hygienic evaluation of these products and materials.The purpose of the study was to substantiate methodological approaches for measuring electrostatic field strength in the vicinity of polymeric material surfaces.Materials and methods. The electrostatic field strength of a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) fabric specimen was measured both at rest and after undergoing a series of rubbing cycles involving various materials.Results. The measured electrostatic field strength values did not exceed established hygienic limits and ranged from 1.04 ± 0.20 to 8.70 ± 1.54 kV/m, depending on the number of rubbing cycles. When the specimen was subjected to friction with synthetic textile materials, the results demonstrated greater stability compared to those obtained with natural wool fabric. Limitations. The findings of this study are applicable exclusively to measurements of electrostatic field strength from synthetic polymer materials conducted under controlled laboratory conditions.Conclusi
