title: High-Resolution Modelling of Coronae and Winds in Solar-type Stars with Varying Rotation Rates II. Stellar Winds
abstract: Observations suggest a connection between steady-wind mass loss and coronal X-ray activity in low-mass main-sequence stars. Interpreting this connection is challenging because the wind is controlled mainly by the large-scale open field, whereas X-ray emission traces heating in small-scale closed fields often unresolved in global wind models. Here we use Space Weather Modelling Framework-Alfvén-Wave Solar Model with global convective dynamo-generated magnetic maps and solar magnetograms. We model Alfvén-wave-heated winds for four solar-type stars plus the Sun, spanning rotation rates of $1.0$--$23.3$ times the solar rate, and magnetic field strengths of $6.0$--$1200$ G. Our models show that faster rotation yields a more tightly wound spiral, a larger Alfvén surface, higher terminal wind speeds, and a harsher wind-pressure environment for orbiting exoplanets, different from that of the present-day Sun. We estimate the mass- and angular-momentum-loss rates and find systematic differences from Zeeman-Doppler Imaging-based predictions. Building on the successful reproduction of X-ray coronae in our Paper~I, we obtain the first self-consistent activity--wind relation in a unified modelling framework: the mass-loss rate scales with the surface X-ray flux following a power law with an index of ${\sim}0.67$. title: Machine Learning Application for Reciprocating Compressor Performance Prediction Under Varying Suction Pressures: A Case Study on Gas Pipeline Pump-Back Operations
abstract: Abstract During gas pipeline maintenance, degassing is required to maintain operational safety and to support integrity and corrosion monitoring. Flaring is commonly used for this purpose, but it creates emissions and can trigger regulatory challenges. As an alternative, a skid-mounted reciprocating compressor can recover the gas and redirect it back into the pipeline. However, during pump-back operations the suction pressure often declines continuously. This causes compressor capacity and power demand to vary over time, which complicates scheduling and cost estimation. This study develops machine-learning fast proxy models to predict reciprocating compressor performance under variable suction pressures using a structured performance dataset generated with the Ariel Performance Program for a representative pump-back case. After cleaning and numeric consistency checks, the dataset contains 3111 operating points spanning 61 suction-pressure conditions (50 - 350 psig) and discharge pressures of ∼750 - 1000 psig, with flow ranging ∼0.4 - 3.0 MMSCFD and brake horsepower (BHP) ranging ∼82 - 223 BHP. Two independent machine learning models were trained, one for flow and one for BHP, using suction pressure, discharge pressure, and compressor speed (fixed at 1800 RPM for all cases) augmented with physics-informed features (ΔP, compression ratio, and ln(compression ratio)). title: DEVELOPMENT AND EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH OF A POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM FOR A AUTOTRACTOR DIESEL ENGINE FOR OPERATION IN GAS-DIESEL MODE ON LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
abstract: Modernization and conversion of agricultural machinery to alternative fuels is a key tool for improv-ing its environmental and economic performance. The use of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in dual-fuel systems allows for a significant reduction in emissions of harmful substances (CO2, CO, NOx), however, the successful conversion of serial tractor diesel engines with the provision of stable operational characteristics at all load modes remains an unsolved scientific and practical prob-lem. The purpose of the work is to develop methods and techniques for experimental research of a diesel engine in a gasodiesel cycle, which ensures its stable operation at various load-speed modes with different fuel mixture compositions. To implement the tasks set, an original schematic diagram of the gas-diesel engine power supply system with a mechanical device for manual adjustment of the position of the high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) rail of the UTN-5 type was developed, which made it possible to eliminate the instabil-ity of the standard all-mode regulator. Experimental studies were carried out on a KI-5542 brake running-in stand based on a four-cylinder diesel engine 4F11.0/12.5, additionally equipped with gas cylinder equipment, a panel rotameter LZM-15ZT-4 and an electronic gas flow weight control sys-tem. title: "Development of a Multi-Source Energy Harvesting System and Embedded EMS Software for Self-Sustaining Electric Vehicles"
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: बहु-स्रोत ऊर्जा संचयन और हाइब्रिड चार्जिंग सिस्टम युक्त स्व-संचालित वाहन (Self-Sustaining Vehicle)आविष्कारकर्ता का नाम: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)1. आविष्कार का परिचय (Introduction)यह आविष्कार एक अत्याधुनिक, पर्यावरण-अनुकूल और आत्मनिर्भर हाइब्रिड वाहन (Self-Sustaining Electric Vehicle) से संबंधित है, जो प्रकृति में मौजूद ऊर्जा संरक्षण के नियम (Law of Conservation of Energy) पर आधारित है। ऊर्जा संरक्षण के नियम के अनुसार, "ऊर्जा को न तो नष्ट किया जा सकता है और न ही उत्पन्न किया जा सकता है, इसे केवल एक रूप से दूसरे रूप में बदला जा सकता है।"इस सिद्धांत का उपयोग करते हुए, यह गाड़ी किसी एक ईंधन (जैसे पेट्रोल, डीजल या बाहरी चार्जिंग स्टेशन) पर निर्भर रहने के बजाय अपने आस-पास की विभिन्न ऊर्जाओं को इकट्ठा (Harvest) करती है। यह वाहन एक साथ चार अलग-अलग स्रोतों से बिजली बनाकर अपनी बैटरी को चार्ज करता है और इसमें लगा एक विशेष सॉफ्टवेयर (Energy Management System) इस पूरी प्रक्रिया को नियंत्रित करता है। 2. आविष्कार की मुख्य विशेषताएं और तकनीकी फॉर्मूलावाहन को निरंतर ऊर्जा प्रदान करने के लिए इसमें निम्नलिखित घटकों और तकनीकों का संयोजन किया गया है:पूर्ण सोलर स्किन तकनीक (Full Solar Skin Body): वाहन का केवल ऊपरी हिस्सा ही नहीं, बल्कि इसकी पूरी बाहरी बॉडी विशेष 'सोलर स्किन' (Integrated Photovoltaic Cells) से ढकी होगी। यह तकनीक सूरज की सीधी धूप के साथ-साथ रात में सड़क की स्ट्रीट लाइट या घर/लैब के अंदर जलने वाले बल्ब की रोशनी से भी ऊर्जा (Micro-watts) सोखने में सक्षम है।ड्रोन आधारित माइक्रो-टर्बाइन सिस्टम (Drone-Inspired Micro-Turbines): वाहन की गति में बाधा (Aerodynamic Drag) डाले बिना हवा से ब

title: Coupled Field-Based Design Optimization Brake Discs Rotor for Braking System
abstract: Efficient thermal management and structural integrity are essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of automotive braking systems. Conventional grey cast iron brake disc rotors, while widely adopted, often suffer from limitations such as high thermal stresses, localized deformation, and insufficient heat dissipation under severe braking conditions. These shortcomings can lead to reduced braking efficiency, premature wear, and compromised durability. The current study examines the thermo-mechanical performance of a grey cast iron brake disc rotor through geometry-based optimization using finite element modeling. The objective is to improve heat transfer capability and the mechanical strength under transient braking load without changing the composition of the material used. A comparative analysis is conducted between the optimized model and three other benchmark models under various speeds from 800 rpm to 2000 rpm. It was found that the optimized rotor is able to reduce its maximum temperature by up to 22.5% with an improvement greater than 30% at low rotational speeds. Moreover, it has reduced Von Mises stress of about 18–25% and total deformation by 15–20% in comparison with benchmark models. This enhanced behavior can be attributed to better placement of slots and holes, leading to better convective heat transfer and minimizing temperature gradient. In addition, a more uniform heat flux distribution is observed, reducing localized hotspots and stress concentrations.

title: Prognostic Thermal Modeling and Control of a Carbon–Ceramic Brake Disc for Electric Sports Cars under Racetrack Conditions
journal: SAE International Journal of Electrified Vehicles
abstract: Carbon–ceramic brake discs in high-performance electric sports cars are vulnerable to heat fade under racetrack conditions, where repeated high-speed braking can raise disc temperature above the material’s safe limit of 1200°C. Three-dimensional finite-volume analysis is accurate but inefficient for long transient track events. To improve efficiency, a one-dimensional lumped capacitance method (LCM) is proposed to predict brake disc temperature evolution. A speed-dependent cooling coefficient links disc thermal response to vehicle operating conditions. The model is validated against wheel-end temperature measurements of sports cars on the Zhuzhou International Circuit and Nürburgring Nordschleife Circuit. It is then used to assess three thermal control measures: an external air director, increased disc thermal mass, and higher regenerative braking contribution. The model reproduces the measured trend with acceptable error and predicts that the baseline disc temperature can peak at 1445°C in a four-lap Zhuzhou scenario and 1540°C in a Nürburgring scenario. The air director provides substantial cooling but is insufficient on its own. A system-level safe temperature of 1050°C is achieved only when the disc size is increased to 410 mm × 40 mm and regenerative braking deceleration is raised to at least 0.1 g in combination with the air director scheme. The proposed LCM provides a practical and computationally efficient tool for early-stage brake thermal design of sports cars.

title: Topology Optimization of Brake Disc Inner Carrier and Development of a Parametric Predictive Model Using Machine Learning
abstract: Reducing unsprung mass in high-performance braking systems is critical for vehicle dynamics, but applying topology optimization (TO) to conventional solid discs under combined thermo-mechanical loading often causes “thermal entrapment” and structural failure. This study addresses this limitation by proposing a floating disc architecture and a two-stage computational framework. First, TO via the SIMP algorithm was applied to the Aluminum 7075-T6 inner carrier strictly under mechanical loads, decoupling artificial thermal stresses and yielding a fixed, optimized geometry. Results show the TO achieved a drastic 53% mass reduction (from 0.218 kg to 0.102 kg) specifically for the inner carrier component. Second, a high-fidelity Surrogate Model (Digital Twin) of this new geometry was developed to bypass the immense computational cost of multi-parameter, non-linear thermo-mechanical Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Utilizing Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) across 15 design scenarios and the Genetic Aggregation algorithm, the surrogate model was trained to predict real-time responses. Subsequently, the Digital Twin predicted stress and temperature fields with near-perfect accuracy (R2≈0.9998), rapidly identifying the limit braking scenario. Fatigue analysis confirmed the final component safely withstands 106 extreme braking cycles (safety factor 1.65).

title: Transient thermal modeling and experimental assessment of a variable-gap multi-disc magnetorheological brake with nonuniform working gaps
abstract: Abstract Thermal accumulation limits continuous-duty performance of compact multi-disc magnetorheological (MR) brakes. A three-dimensional transient thermal model for a variable-gap brake with nonuniform gaps is evaluated using infrared thermography, thermocouples, and passive-cooling tests. MR fluid shear dissipation and coil Joule heating are treated as internal heat sources, with conduction through the assembly and convection at external boundaries. Three independent tests were conducted for each repeatability condition. At zero bracket displacement, the mean probe temperature at 300 s increased from 46.08 °C at 40 N·m to 61.37 °C at 70 N·m; sample standard deviations were 0.60 °C–0.91 °C and coefficients of variation were 1.31%–1.59%. Probe-temperature comparisons at 40 and 60 N·m yielded root-mean-square errors (RMSE) of 0.45 and 0.77 °C, respectively, while the passive-cooling error was 0.74 °C. At 120 rpm and 60 N·m, the predicted internal hotspot reached 94.7 °C, whereas measured external temperatures were approximately 49 °C–51 °C. Increasing bracket displacement from 0 to 3.5 mm reduced the predicted peak temperature to 59.9 °C and improved internal temperature uniformity, although the measured outer-region temperature increased from 48.98 °C to 55.95 °C because of heat redistribution. title: Numerical study of the influence of duct cross-section geometry on flow characteristics and brake cooling performance in a heavy-duty bus
journal: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
publisher: Society of Polish Mechanical Engineers and Technicians
abstract: Efficient heat dissipation during braking is crucial for maintaining the performance and reliability of brake systems in heavy-duty vehicles.Although CFD has been widely applied to brake thermal analysis, the isolated influence of brake cooling duct cross-sectional geometry on airflow characteristics and convective cooling performance has received limited attention.This study numerically evaluated the influence of duct cross-sectional geometry on the flow characteristics and cooling performance of a heavy-duty bus brake system using two consecutive computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models implemented in ANSYS CFX.First, circular and square cross-section ducts were analyzed for vehicle speeds of 60, 90, and 120 km/h to determine the outlet flow conditions.Subsequently, these flow conditions were used as inlet boundary conditions for the thermal analysis of a brake disc subjected to surface temperatures of 600, 700, and 800 K.The numerical reliability of the simulations was verified through mesh independence analyses, where successive mesh refinements produced variations below 0.5% in the monitored variables.The results showed that the circular duct generated higher exit velocities than the square duct under all analyzed conditions, reaching 51.88 m/s and 39.52 m/s, respectively, at 90 km/h.Although this improvement was accompanied by greater pressure losses, the circular configuration increased the brake disc heat dissipation by approximately 51% at a surface temperature of 6

title: An Open-Source Reduced-Scale Test Bench for Flywheel-Assisted Regenerative Braking in Electric Vehicles
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This repository provides the open-source resources associated with the design, construction, and experimental evaluation of a low-cost, reduced-scale test bench for investigating flywheel-assisted regenerative braking in electric vehicles. The experimental platform consists of two direct-current (DC) motor-generators coupled to interchangeable steel discs that represent vehicle-equivalent inertia and flywheel energy storage. A configurable power circuit incorporating electromechanical relays, MOSFET-based switching stages, and a DC–DC boost converter enables the investigation of different operating modes, including freewheeling, regenerative braking, dynamic braking, and battery-assisted braking. An Arduino Nano microcontroller performs operating-mode selection, speed measurement, battery-voltage and current acquisition, and communication with a host computer. The repository includes mechanical design files, electrical schematics and PCB design resources, firmware, component information, and experimental data supporting the reported proof-of-concept evaluation using a scaled and temporally extended reference derived from the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS). The platform is intended as an accessible and reconfigurable experimental environment for developing, implementing, and comparing braking-control and energy-management strategies. Its modular design also supports the investigation of different inertia configurations and future extensions involving alternative ene

title: Exploring LLMs and RAG for Plausible and Explainable Material Prediction of Vehicle Components
abstract: In this work, we explore whether LLMs can accurately predict and explain plausible materials for vehicle components such as brake discs or fuel injectors without requiring extensive fine-tuning. We test and evaluate three approaches: a standard generative LLM baseline, a single-pass Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach, and an iterative Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) variant. For retrieval, we rely on publicly available data using a domain-filtered Wikipedia corpus. Since no gold standard exists for this task, we develop a custom web-based annotation tool supporting crucial functions for structured domain expert evaluation. LLM-based generation substantially outperforms prior work, which is not further surpassed by the tested RAG approaches. Our results surface remaining challenges for RAG-based systems: hyperparameter optimization, the availability of high-quality, legally accessible domain corpora, and expert evaluation study design.

title: Development of a Computer Simulation Model of a Passenger Train for Studying Traction and Energy Processes Based on Motion Parameter Recording Systems
abstract: tehnicheskogo obsluzhivaniya tormoznogo oborudovaniya i upravleniya tormozami zheleznodorozhnogo podvizhnogo sostava [Rules for Maintenance of Brake Equipment and Brake Control for Railway Rolling Stock], approved by the Council for Railway Transport of the CIS Member States, of regenerated energy to the overhead contact system. Dependencies of braking force on pressure in brake cylinders have been obtained for tread and disc brakes. Verification of the model was carried out by comparing simulation results with full-scale experimental data; it was established that the error in calculating speed, energy consumption and energy recovery does not exceed 2 %. Practical significance: the developed model can be used to analyze train handling patterns applied by locomotive crews and automated systems, assess energy efficiency, improve traffic safety and enhance the operation technologies of traction rolling stock.

title: Design and analysis of a hybrid FRP/metal freight bogie for improved performance and functionality
abstract: Although replacing conventional metallic freight bogies with fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) alternatives has attracted substantial research interest, practical implementation remains limited due to technical and economic constraints. This study proposes a hybrid bogie concept combining flexible FRP side beams with a metallic bolster to improve functional integration and mass efficiency. By integrating multifunctional FRP components and applying a load-path-driven design approach, the concept extends beyond simple material substitution. Structural integrity and operational performance are assessed using finite element analysis and multibody running dynamics simulations. The results indicate adequate stiffness and stress levels under representative loads, as well as stable, derailment-safe running behavior. Relative to the conventional Y25 freight bogie, the present design yields an estimated mass reduction of approximately 500 kg per bogie, including disc brakes, and shows promising stability and steering performance in simulations. A reduced part count and efficient use of FRP materials are expected to improve life-cycle cost competitiveness compared with conventional bogie designs, while the integration of disc brakes within a significantly lighter bogie concept provides a pathway toward low-noise freight bogies.

title: Supporting data for Design of a Direct-Drive Axle-Mounted Traction Motor for Boosting High-Speed Trains
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This dataset accompanies the article “Design of a Direct-Drive Axle-Mounted Traction Motor for Boosting High-Speed Trains”. It provides selected non-confidential design inputs, simulation conditions, processed numerical results and derived calculations for a direct-drive permanent magnet synchronous motor designed for supplementary high-speed railway traction within the available wheel-to-axlebox installation envelope while retaining the existing disc-brake hardware. The Excel workbook contains ten worksheets: Guide, Results, Configuration, Electromagnetic, Thermal, Mechanical, Masses, Topology, MODE_selection and Benchmark. They document the disclosed motor configuration, electromagnetic and thermal assessments, structural analyses, component masses and power densities, topology refinement, multiobjective optimisation settings and duty-cycle benchmarking. Data origins and relevant assumptions are identified within the worksheets. Performance results are numerical predictions or design calculations rather than prototype performance measurements. Preliminary optimisation results and final detailed-design results represent different design stages and should not be treated as interchangeable. title: AAU Rotor Vibration Dataset Under Time-Varying Speed Scenarios
abstract: Rotors are always operated under time-varying rotational speed conditions, and variable-speed fault datasets of the rotor are adopted to support the investigation of evolutionary mechanisms throughout fault initiation, propagation and failure. In this data article, rotor vibration datasets are collected with different health conditions under time-varying speed conditions. The health conditions of the rotor include normal condition, groove failure, wear failure, broken failure and bending failure. The configuration of the experimental setup mainly consists of a three-phase asynchronous motor, variable frequency drive, shaft coupling, double-support bearings with type PH205, rotor disc, reducer gearbox, magnetic powder brake, etc. The rotational speed datasets are measured using a photoelectric speed sensor. Vibration signals are acquired with a piezoelectric accelerometer with sampling frequency of 20 kHz . The experiments are conducted under constant load torque of 4 N · m with a rotational-speed range of 0-1200 r/min. The accelerometer was mounted on the right side of the rotor disk. The operating rotational speed conditions contain both steady-speed and variable-speed rotor vibration samples. The variable-speed working profiles are designed to simulate the typical speed transition processes encountered in practical industrial systems. title: An investigation of advanced design techniques for improved mixed flow turbine efficiency
abstract: With ever increasing pressure for decarbonisation of the internal combustion engine, engine brake thermal efficiency is of great importance. Turbocharging has been used for many years to facilitate an increase in specific power, and subsequent engine downsizing, which in turn is used to increase the efficiency of the engine installation. Considering the decarbonisation goal, it is imperative that efficiency is at the forefront of each component within the system. This includes the turbocharger. Considering the maturity of turbocharger turbines, the drive for increased efficiency is challenging. This thesis details two research studies which aimed to facilitate a step change in efficiency. The first study detailed an evaluation of truly three dimensional rotor blading. In this study, the ubiquitous radial fibre constraint was relaxed, with a numerical optimisation exercise used to explore a truly three dimensional design space. A new design approach was detailed, which leveraged the aerodynamically insensitive hub region to automatically adapt to 3D geometries and mitigate against the effects of non-radially fibred blading. Through the novel design approach, a new 3D geometry was identified which offered a performance improvement across the entire turbocharger operating line of 1.1% as predicted by CFD simulations without compromising mechanical integrity. title: The Dopamine Brain: Wanting: Why You Chase What You Don't Enjoy
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Dopamine was never the pleasure chemical. It hands you the urge to go and get something, and wanting and liking come apart. The Dopamine Brain is about the circuit that decides what a person will cross a room for, and what the modern food supply, the modern phone and the modern pharmacy have taught it. The book starts with what dopamine actually encodes: prediction error, vigor and the drive to act rather than enjoyment. It follows the molecule from synthesis to its receptors and into movement, then out of the brain into its lesser-known jobs: the brake on prolactin, the dopamine the gut makes for itself, nausea, blood pressure, immunity, and its crosstalk with insulin and calorie sensing. It then takes on the drugs that imitate or block it, from dopamine agonists, trace amines and stimulants to antipsychotic blockade and the opioid detour, before turning to the hedonic treadmill, the lonely striatum, the sleep-starved receptor, the anti-reward system and the loop between pain and dopamine. It closes on movement as the prescription and on hedonic substitution. Each chapter ends with two codes, one for a Deep Dive evidence briefing written to be handed to the reader's own physician and one for the chapter's video. title: Experimental Investigation of Torque and Vibration Characteristics of Rotating Shafts Under Controlled Misalignment
journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
abstract: Accurate torque measurement and vibration monitoring are essential for assessing the performance and condition of rotating machinery; however, conventional torque sensors are often intrusive, costly, and difficult to integrate into existing systems. This study presents an integrated experimental and data-driven framework for investigating the relationship between transmitted torque and vibration characteristics of rotating shafts under aligned and controlled angular misalignment conditions. A customized experimental test rig incorporating interchangeable steel shafts, non-contact optical encoders, accelerometers, and a magnetic powder brake dynamometer was developed. Experiments were conducted over a torque range of 20–100 Nm using shaft diameters of 10–14 mm, shaft lengths of 0.5–0.7 m, and angular misalignment levels from 0° to 2°. Torque was estimated from the encoder-measured angular twist using classical torsion theory, while synchronized vibration signals were analysed using statistical and entropy-based features, including root mean square (RMS), standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, Shannon entropy, and spectral entropy. Supervised machine-learning models were subsequently employed to investigate vibration-based indirect torque estimation, with performance assessed using R², RMSE, and MAE. title: Integrated Energy Management Strategy for Battery Life Extension in Electric Vehicle Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Using an Enhanced Multiport Bidirectional Converter
abstract: Hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) combining batteries and ultracapacitors (UCs) can improve the performance and lifespan of electric vehicle (EV) energy storage systems. Their effectiveness depends on the selected multiport converter and energy management strategy (EMS), which play key roles in reducing battery stress and improving longevity. Accordingly, this paper proposes an enhanced multiport converter employing a bidirectional converter for the UC and a unidirectional converter for the battery, enabling bidirectional power transfer among the battery, UC and load through flexible and reconfigurable power-flow paths. An integrated EMS is proposed to provide transient power support during motoring, prioritize UC charging during regenerative braking and initiate C-rate-limited battery charging only after the UC reaches its upper state-of-charge (SoC) limit. The proposed system is evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS), while the converter operation is experimentally demonstrated using a laboratory prototype. The simulation results demonstrate a 77.5% reduction in peak battery charging current, 12% reduction in RMS battery charging current and 68.7% reduction in battery charging occurrences compared with the conventional EMS. Furthermore, the proposed EMS increases the regenerative braking energy absorbed by the UC by 36.1%. The comparative battery aging analysis indicates a 58.6% increase in estimated Ah-throughput.
